launch_events: Phase I: autonomous self-test, N2 blanket pressure verified in GP-300 cells, BMS and motor-controller pre-ignition checks

MECO (FCU velocity threshold) at 55.2 km, 2083 m/s

Stage separation: pneumatic latches released, break-wire confirmed; Vibhu vacuum engine start, star trackers in the GNC loop
Booster 180 deg flip on gaseous RCS complete; Shakti subset re-ignites (propellant settling monitored)
Divert burn complete (150 m/s, cut-off error +3.0 m/s); barge on station 491.9 km downrange (design touchdown point)
Drag fins open at 100 km: 4 panels on the base ring to 32 deg, drag area x2.05; fin encoders and FBG strain network logging
SECO-1: transfer orbit 125 x 579 km, coasting to apogee (162 kg propellant left)

Landing burn at 1.1 km, 165 m/s; radar + LiDAR altimeters take the vertical loop below 2 km

Booster landed on the barge, gear Hall-effect locks confirmed at 3.8 m/s, 3 m from the deck centre, 492 km downrange, prop remaining 300 kg; recovery dv used boostback 150, entry_burn 1001, landing_burn 303 m/s; peak 3.4 g, peak heating 58 kW/m2
SECO-2: orbit 581 x 637 km, 118 kg propellant margin
Orbit insertion confirmed, LELP + upper stage nominal

ret_events: Integrated upper stage deorbit burn, 150 m/s retrograde with the whole lab attached: perigee 29 km, entry interface in 33 min

Dexter-L turns its ring to the gap between two module columns, reaches down the outside of the stack to the grapple post on the upper stage, latches on and releases its own base latch: the arm does not come home
Return Module separates; the upper stage takes Dexter-L, the solar wings and the ISL antenna (20 kg) with it, is passivated, and breaks up over open sea about 500 km beyond the recovery zone
Inflatable heat shield deploying: 4 stacked tori, 1.1 m packed to 2.6 m in 90 s, nitrogen at 1 bar gauge
Entry interface at 120 km, 7.9 km/s, flight-path angle -1.7 deg; 223 kg behind a 2.6 m aeroshell, ballistic coefficient 26 kg/m2
Peak heating 434 kW/m2 at 74 km, 6.6 km/s on the flexible TPS; peak 7.7 g at 61 km; radio blackout 2 min 8 s
Main parachute at 4 km, 25 m/s under the aeroshell; 9 m ringsail, reefed fill in 6 s
Splashdown at 7.9 m/s on the inflated aeroshell, which cushions the impact and floats the lab; Bay of Bengal, 2.6 km from the recovery ship
Lab and aeroshell craned aboard the recovery ship 19 min after splashdown; all 32 modules on board
